purpose: Evaluation-only material comparison. Materially different substances are never equated.

sources.role: authoritative supported-material vocabulary and appearance-vs-fact certainty rules
second supported-material list; divergence documented below

families._comment: Parent families are EVALUATION-ONLY groupings. Production has no material family map — only the flat SUPPORTED_MATERIALS set and the normalizeMaterial collapses below. Every parent here is marked with its justification.

cotton_family.justification: normalizeMaterial collapses knit/ribbed/jersey -> 'knit' but leaves cotton variants distinct. Grouping is evaluation-only.

wool_family.justification: IMPORTED, NOT INVENTED: normalizeMaterial explicitly collapses /(wool|cashmere|tweed)/ -> 'wool/wool blend'. This family reproduces a real production relation.

animal_hide.justification: Evaluation-only. Production keeps leather and suede distinct and normalizeMaterial has separate branches for each.

explicitNonEquivalences.rule: NEVER equivalent. faux leather belongs to 'synthetic'; leather belongs to 'animal_hide'.
explicitNonEquivalences.productionBasis: normalizeMaterial matches faux/vegan/pu/synthetic leather FIRST and explicitly excludes them from the 'leather' branch. commerceRelevanceColorMaterial comments: 'never invent faux from uncertain leather'.
explicitNonEquivalences.scoring: Predicting 'leather' where ground truth is 'faux leather' is INCORRECT, not acceptably_broad. The reverse is also INCORRECT.
explicitNonEquivalences.severity: This is a material misrepresentation with commercial consequence, not a vocabulary nicety.

explicitNonEquivalences.productionBasis: APPEARANCE_SYNONYMS maps suede-like/suede-look -> 'suede' for FALLBACK QUERIES ONLY, with certainty 'appearance_only'. That is a search-expansion allowance, not a factual equivalence.
explicitNonEquivalences.scoring: Scored incorrect. The appearance synonym is NOT imported as a truth relation.

explicitNonEquivalences.rule: Not equivalent, and denim is NOT given a parent.
explicitNonEquivalences.productionBasis: normalizeMaterial has a dedicated exact branch: lower === 'denim' -> 'denim'. Denim is never folded into cotton anywhere in production, despite being a cotton twill in fact.
explicitNonEquivalences.governedParentDecision: denim is a TERMINAL family with no parent, determined from the existing taxonomy as required. Assigning it cotton_family would create a broader-credit path production does not recognize.

explicitNonEquivalences.rule: Same family (wool_family) by production's own collapse, so cashmere(GT) vs wool(pred) is acceptably_broad.

certaintyClasses._comment: Imported from production MaterialCertainty. Governs whether a material claim is factual or appearance-only.
certaintyClasses.supported: Value is in SUPPORTED_MATERIALS. Scored normally.
certaintyClasses.likely: Provider hedged (likely|probably|possibly|appears|seems|maybe). Scored as a hedged claim: correct value -> correct; wrong value -> incorrect but NOT unsupported_certainty, because the model signalled doubt.
certaintyClasses.appearance_only: Matched APPEARANCE_MATERIAL_RE (leather-look, suede-like, ...). Never scored as a factual material claim.
certaintyClasses.unsupported: Matched UNSUPPORTED_MATERIAL_RE (lambskin, calfskin, exotic, python, ostrich, designer, luxury). A specific claim here against an unknown label is unsupported_certainty.

productionDivergence.detail: commerceRelevanceColorMaterial SUPPORTED_MATERIALS contains 'wool' and 'wool blend' as separate entries; scannerQualityGate contains both 'wool/wool blend' (the compound normalizeMaterial output) and 'wool'.
productionDivergence.resolution: Evaluation accepts all three surface forms and resolves them to wool_family. Neither production list is modified.

unsupportedComparisons.reason: No production field carries composition ratios. Not labeled, not scored.

The V2 result exposes item.material as a string ARRAY, not a scalar. Evaluation scores it as a set with the primary (first) element compared for the scalar material label; the full set is retained for reporting. Order is provider-dependent and never scored.
